skill.name: performance-profiler
skill.description: Reviews code for performance bottlenecks such as N+1 queries, inefficient loops, memory leaks, slow algorithms, frontend rendering issues, network overhead, and database inefficiencies.
skill.summary: Finds common code performance bottlenecks and suggests focused fixes.
skill.author: CrazyDubya

content.value_statement: Slow applications are hard to improve without a clear list of bottlenecks. This skill reviews code for query, algorithm, memory, frontend, network, and profiling issues.
actual_capabilities: Identifies N+1 query patterns and recommends joins, eager loading, indexes, pagination, and query limits.
Reviews loops and data structures for avoidable O(n^2) behavior.
Checks frontend code for re-render, bundle size, lazy loading, image, and memoization issues.
Lists memory leak risks such as uncleared timers, retained listeners, circular references, and unbounded caches.
Produces prioritized performance reports with issue impact and suggested fixes.
Points users toward profiling tools for JavaScript, Python, and databases.
limitations: It does not run benchmarks or profilers.
It depends on the code and context provided by the user.
It may miss runtime issues that are only visible under production load.
It provides recommendations, not guaranteed performance improvements.

use_cases.title: Review Database Query Performance
use_cases.description: Find query patterns that increase latency, including N+1 queries, missing indexes, wide selects, and missing pagination.

use_cases.title: Reduce UI Rendering Cost
use_cases.description: Check frontend components for unnecessary rerenders, bundle size issues, missing lazy loading, and expensive UI operations.

use_cases.title: Prepare Performance Review Notes
use_cases.description: Create a prioritized report that explains impact, suggested fixes, and profiling tools for release readiness reviews.

prompt_templates.title: Find Obvious Bottlenecks
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner review of a small code sample.
prompt_templates.prompt: Review this code for clear performance issues. Focus on queries, loops, memory leaks, and frontend rendering problems.

prompt_templates.title: Prioritize a Slow Feature
prompt_templates.scenario: Intermediate review of a known slow workflow.
prompt_templates.prompt: Analyze the attached feature for performance bottlenecks. Rank issues by user impact, implementation effort, and confidence.

prompt_templates.title: Compare Optimization Options
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced review of multiple possible fixes.
prompt_templates.prompt: Review these proposed optimizations. Explain trade-offs, expected gains, and risks for maintainability.

prompt_templates.title: Create a Profiling Plan
prompt_templates.prompt: Build a profiling plan for this service. Include hypotheses, metrics, tools, expected evidence, and follow-up fixes.

output_examples.input: A controller loads users and then fetches posts inside a loop.
output: Flags the N+1 pattern as high priority.
Recommends eager loading or a single joined query.
Explains the request impact as the user count grows.

output_examples.input: A React list rerenders when filters change.
output: Suggests memoization only where it reduces measured work.
Recommends virtual scrolling for long result sets.

output_examples.input: A team wants a performance review before launch.
output: Groups findings by critical, high, and medium priority.
Connects each issue to expected user impact.
Adds profiling tools that can verify the assumptions.

best_practices: Profile before changing code so fixes target measured bottlenecks.
Prioritize hot paths and high-traffic workflows before rare cases.
Measure before and after each change to confirm real improvement.
anti_patterns: Optimizing code without a measured problem.
Adding caching without invalidation, limits, or ownership.
Trading clear code for minor performance gains without evidence.

faq.question: Does this skill execute profiling tools?
faq.answer: No. It guides review and recommends tools, but it only uses reading and search capabilities.

faq.question: Can it review database performance?
faq.answer: Yes. It looks for N+1 queries, missing indexes, wide selects, pagination gaps, and inefficient joins.

faq.question: Can it find memory leaks?
faq.answer: It can identify common leak patterns, including retained listeners, uncleared timers, circular references, and unbounded caches.

faq.question: Does it support frontend projects?
faq.answer: Yes. It covers React rendering issues, bundle size, image optimization, code splitting, and list rendering patterns.

faq.question: Will it guarantee faster code?
faq.answer: No. It provides likely fixes and profiling guidance, but real results require measurement.

faq.question: Which assistants can use it?
faq.answer: The report lists support for Claude, Codex, and Claude Code.
